sections.html:
Kaysville is in Davis County, part of the Ogden-Clearfield metro area, with Layton to the north, Fruit Heights to the east and Farmington to the south. The 2020 census counted 32,945 residents in 8,958 households and 9,175 housing units. Just 2.4% of those units were vacant, so an empty or neglected house stands out on a street where neighbors live next door all year.

Families dominate the city: the median age is 29.9, and about 52.4% of households are raising children under 18. A house that sits empty after an owner moves away or passes on can look out of step with its block, and the carrying costs keep running in the meantime.

sections.h2: Jobs, commuting and moving on a deadline
sections.html:
Davis County is largely a bedroom community, and many residents commute into Salt Lake County. Hill Air Force Base at the north end of the county is the largest employer, followed by the Davis School District, Lagoon Amusement Park and Lifetime Products. People who relocate for work often need a sale with a closing date they can plan around.

  • If you are moving for a job, ask any buyer to confirm the closing date in writing.
  • A house that must be vacated before a move can be sold as it stands, without staging.
  • Heirs who live out of state can finish a sale through a title company without traveling to Kaysville.

The Davis School District serves Kaysville, and Davis High School is the city's high school. The city supplies garbage pickup, curbside recycling, green waste recycling, power, pressure irrigation, storm water and water. Sewer comes from Central Davis Sewer instead of the city. Kaysville City Power is at 721 W Old Mill Lane, phone 801-544-8925, which is the number to use when you transfer power in a sale.

Kaysville bases permit fees on project value, adds a 1% state education fee and a 25% plan check fee, and posts a fee schedule online. Impact fees apply to new single-family homes, and a few typical amounts are below.

Permit or feeKaysville amount
Parks and recreation impact fee, new home$4,480
Central Davis Sewer fee, new home$2,400
North Davis Sewer fee, new home$3,454.03
Basement finish or remodel permit$245.70
Furnace, A/C or water heater permit$65.65
Pool permit$260 plus a $500 bond

A permit expires if work has not started within 180 days or stops for 180 days, and the construction bond is forfeited. A seller with a half-finished basement and an expired permit may find that a buyer with a mortgage wants it closed out first. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands and sort out the permit afterward.

sections.h2: Can I rent out part of my Kaysville house?
sections.html:
Kaysville allows internal accessory dwelling units, provided the owner lives in the main home or the unit as a primary residence. The rules are in Kaysville City Code 17-31-3.

  • A permit is required when someone who is not a related family member will live in the unit.
  • The unit needs its own paved parking space on top of the two-car garage and two-car driveway.
  • Detached structures, such as an apartment over a garage or a granny flat, cannot be used as a dwelling.
  • Additions or remodels done to create the unit need a building permit.

If you bought a house with a basement apartment, confirm it was set up under these rules. A house rented out in full with an apartment inside may not qualify, since the owner has to live there.

Davis County mails valuation notices at the end of July. State law sets the appeal deadline as the later of September 15 or 45 days after the auditor provides the notice, so call Tax Administration to confirm the exact date before you file.

Only market value can be appealed, not the tax rate. The Davis County Commission serves as the Board of Equalization and relies on recommendations from hearing officers it appoints. Evidence can include closing documents, a certified appraisal or comparable sales, and an agent filing for an owner needs a notarized authorization.

  • Tax Administration is at 61 South Main Street, Room 101, Farmington.
  • Phone: 801-451-3331 or 801-451-3329.
  • Late appeals go to the Board of Equalization, which may accept them for extenuating circumstances.

Utah's primary residential exemption taxes a qualifying home on 55% of market value. After a sale the new owner has to submit a new application, so tell the buyer to expect that step.

sections.h2: How a cash sale of a Kaysville house works
sections.html:
A cash sale closes at a title company, and the deed is recorded with the Davis County Recorder. With no loan involved, the steps are a purchase contract, a title search, signatures on a settlement statement and recording of the deed.

Utah law requires a deed to name the grantees, give a mailing address for assessment and taxation, and include a legal description that meets state standards. The recorder may also ask for the tax identification number on the document.

When a house sells mid-year, the title company normally prorates the year's tax at closing, so ask for the proration figure before the closing date.

sections.h2: Situations that call for a quick sale
sections.html:
• Inherited houses that need updating before a conventional listing.
  • Basement apartments set up without a permit or without the required parking space.
  • Expired building permits with a forfeited bond.
  • Owners who must relocate and cannot manage showings from afar.

Whichever route you pick, compare the net amount after repairs, commission and carrying costs, and read any contract before signing.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Davis County?
faqs.a: State law uses the later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice. Call Tax Administration at 801-451-3331 to confirm the date before filing.

faqs.q: Can I put an apartment in my Kaysville basement?
faqs.a: Yes, as an internal accessory dwelling unit, if you live in the main home or the unit. It needs its own paved parking space, and a permit is required if a non-family member will live there.

faqs.q: Who provides sewer service in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Central Davis Sewer provides sewer service, not the city. The city provides water, power, pressure irrigation, garbage, recycling and storm water.

faqs.q: Do building permits expire in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Yes. A permit expires if work does not start within 180 days of issuance or stops for 180 days. The bond is then forfeited and a new application is needed.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kaysville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 32,945 residents, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 33,307.
